method: STRIDE-informed misuse cases with protocol safety outcomes
trustAssumptions: Fabric MSP certificate issuance and private keys are not compromised.
At most one of three assigned Oracles is Byzantine for integrity guarantees.
SHA-256 collision and preimage resistance hold.
Authorized Fabric peers enforce the configured private-data collection policy.
Auditor governance remains available when Oracle consensus fails closed.

threats.name: Single malicious Oracle
threats.attack: Reveal a result that conflicts with two honest workers.
threats.securityProperty: One Byzantine Oracle cannot determine a 2-of-3 decision.
threats.residualRisk: Two colluding assigned Oracles can form a quorum; this is the explicit 2-of-3 trust boundary.

threats.name: Unavailable Oracle
threats.securityProperty: Two available honest Oracles can complete a 2-of-3 decision.
threats.residualRisk: Loss of two workers prevents automatic consensus and requires governed fallback.

threats.name: Conflicting or corrupted registry
threats.attack: Serve records with a root different from the request-bound snapshot.
threats.securityProperty: A mismatched registry root is detected and cannot be reported as VERIFIED.
threats.residualRisk: All replicas derived from the same incorrect source can agree on incorrect data.

threats.name: Forged or unassigned Oracle identity
threats.actor: Fabric client without the assigned Oracle subject
threats.attack: Submit a commitment using a wrong role, missing subject, or unassigned certificate.
threats.securityProperty: Only an assigned OracleMSP certificate subject with the oracle role may vote.
threats.residualRisk: A stolen valid Oracle private key remains able to act until certificate revocation is enforced operationally.

threats.name: Replay or stale Oracle result
threats.attack: Reuse a valid result for another claim version, request, registry, or model.
threats.securityProperty: Changing any adjudication binding changes the canonical digest and stale ledger submissions are rejected.
threats.residualRisk: Compromise before finalization is governed by the quorum assumption rather than replay protection.

threats.name: Altered selective-disclosure proof
threats.attack: Modify a disclosed amount, status, identity, or Merkle path.
threats.securityProperty: Any changed disclosure or proof fails presentation verification.
threats.residualRisk: Authorized Oracle collection members still see disclosed fields; this is selective disclosure, not zero knowledge.

threats.name: Late commitment or reveal
threats.attack: Submit after the commit or reveal deadline to influence the final decision.
threats.securityProperty: Expired phases reject submissions and transition to timeout handling.
threats.residualRisk: A transaction submitted near a deadline can be affected by normal ordering latency.

threats.name: Appeal-version substitution
threats.attack: Attach an old hospital verification or altered appeal fields to a new claim version.
threats.securityProperty: Appeal commitment, claim fields, hospital verification, and version must match exactly.
threats.residualRisk: The correctness of newly submitted source evidence remains an off-chain provenance concern.
